requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.invocation`. The code carries out each obligation and tests exercise each one.

**Syntax and aliasing.**
- `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` declares `Author` with a `subject` argument and the options `--config`, `--missing`, `--force`, `--stdout` and `-v/--verbose`.
- `--missing` conflicts with `--force` and `--stdout`, matching the `[--missing | --force]` syntax.
- `alias = "author-evidence"` provides the alias for the single-subject command.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` runs `author-evidence`. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` also covers the alias with `--all`.
- That test, together with the `--missing`/`--force` conflict checks in the first test, covers the exclusions.
- `--config` is exercised by several `tests/authoring_cli.rs` tests, such as `false_is_a_completed_assessment`.

**Authoring one existing requirement or named example under refresh.**
- `src/main.rs#fn[main]` calls `author_evidence_with_options`.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_options]` applies `refresh`: it forces when `--stdout` is selected, and it returns `None` via `batch::subject_is_current` before resolving configuration.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` rejects a name that is not a requirement or named example with "no matching requirement or named example". A term is rejected the same way.
- `author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets` tests the unknown-subject case.
- The `--missing`/`--force`/`--stdout` behavior is tested in `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject`.

**Completion report (subject, backend, model, evidence destination, usage path).**
- `main` builds "subject: backend / model; policy …" and then prints `Evidence: <path>` and `Usage: <path>`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts the subject and backend prefix, the model, the `Evidence:` line, and that the path ends with `evidence/<subject>.json` and canonicalizes to the project's evidence file. It also asserts the `Usage:` line.

**Evidence destination.**
- By default, `AuthoringOutcome.evidence_path` holds the evidence-file path, and `main` prints it.
- With `--stdout`, `evidence_path` is `None`, and `main` prints "Evidence: stdout".
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` asserts `Evidence: stdout`.

**Stdout mode sends the report and diagnostics to stderr.**
- In stdout mode, `main` prints the report with `eprintln!`. The false-judgment diagnostic and coverage-loss failures also use `eprintln!`, and so does `print_coverage_warnings`.
- Coverage-loss reviews are only populated when records were replaced. `configured_assessment` reads replaced records only in file mode, so stdout mode has none, and the `println!` of their reports is never reached there.
- The stdout test asserts stdout is only the evidence JSON and that the report, usage line and false/FIXME diagnostics appear on stderr. It also checks the verbose rationale there.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
